item.content:encoded:
Artificial Intelligence is transforming industries worldwide, but one of the biggest barriers preventing widespread AI adoption across Africa is the high cost of cloud computing, expensive infrastructure, unstable internet connectivity, and unreliable electricity. To address these challenges, the Africa Deep Tech Foundation (ADTF) has officially launched the Africa Deep Tech Challenge (ADTC) 2026 – The Laptop LLM Challenge, a groundbreaking competition designed to encourage innovators to develop AI systems that run efficiently on affordable laptops already available across the continent.

Rather than rewarding teams for building the largest language models, ADTC 2026 focuses on creating practical, efficient, and locally deployable AI applications capable of running entirely offline. Participants are invited to demonstrate that cutting-edge AI can be accessible, affordable, and useful for millions of people without requiring expensive cloud services or powerful GPUs.

With a total prize pool of $20,000, mentorship opportunities, venture support, GPU credits, and recognition from Africa’s growing deep technology ecosystem, this challenge provides an excellent opportunity for AI developers, researchers, startups, and students to showcase innovative solutions that solve real-world African problems.

Application Deadline: August 25, 2026 (Gate 1 Submission)

What is the Africa Deep Tech Challenge 2026?

The Africa Deep Tech Challenge (ADTC) 2026 is an applied systems engineering competition organized by the Africa Deep Tech Foundation. Unlike traditional AI competitions that emphasize larger models or cloud-hosted systems, this challenge focuses on building practical AI applications capable of operating entirely on consumer-grade laptops commonly used throughout Africa.

The challenge encourages participants to optimize language models so they deliver strong performance while operating under strict hardware limitations. The objective is to democratize access to AI by ensuring advanced language models can function efficiently even where internet connectivity and computational resources are limited.

The competition emphasizes engineering excellence in areas such as:

  • Model quantization
  • Memory optimization
  • Efficient compilation
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
  • Offline knowledge systems
  • Fast inference
  • Responsive user experience
  • Local data integration

The broader vision is to develop AI that people across Africa can own, run, and trust without depending on expensive cloud infrastructure.

Why This Challenge Matters

Across many African countries, accessing cloud-hosted Large Language Models (LLMs) remains expensive due to API costs, internet requirements, and inconsistent electricity.

The Africa Deep Tech Foundation believes the solution is not simply creating larger AI models but engineering smarter systems capable of operating on hardware that millions of Africans already own.

The competition highlights several important challenges:

Limited Access to Cloud AI

Many users cannot rely on continuous internet access or afford subscription-based AI services.

Examples include:

  • University students
  • Healthcare facilities
  • Small businesses
  • Farmers
  • Community organizations
  • Local entrepreneurs

Offline AI significantly reduces these barriers.

AI for Affordable Hardware

Instead of requiring expensive GPUs, the challenge targets affordable laptops costing between $150 and $500, making AI deployment far more accessible.

Efficient AI Engineering

Participants are expected to optimize every aspect of model performance, including:

  • RAM usage
  • Processing speed
  • User experience
  • Memory allocation
  • Model compression
  • Local retrieval systems

Competition Problem Domains

Participants must choose one primary application area while demonstrating at least one meaningful cross-disciplinary integration.

Available domains include:

1. Mathematics and Scientific Reasoning

Possible applications include:

  • Mathematical problem solving
  • Proof assistance
  • Scientific calculations
  • Quantitative reasoning

2. Healthcare and Medical Support

Potential solutions include:

  • Clinical question answering
  • Patient education
  • Healthcare information
  • Medical triage assistance

3. Agriculture

Innovators can develop AI tools that support:

  • Crop management
  • Livestock advisory
  • Weather information
  • Agricultural planning
  • Market intelligence

4. Creative Writing

Possible applications include:

  • Story generation
  • Editing assistance
  • Poetry
  • Multilingual writing
  • Content creation

5. Coding Assistants

Developers may create offline tools capable of:

  • Code generation
  • Debugging
  • Programming tutorials
  • Software development assistance

6. Enterprise Productivity

Business-focused applications may include:

  • Knowledge management
  • Internal documentation
  • SME productivity
  • Workflow support

7. Autonomous AI Agents

Participants can develop intelligent offline agents capable of:

  • Workflow automation
  • Privacy-focused task execution
  • Local orchestration
  • Offline decision support

REGISTER  HERE

Hardware Requirements

Every submission must successfully operate on the official ADTC Standard Laptop.

Target hardware specifications include:

Component Requirement
CPU Intel Core i5 (10th–12th Generation x86-64)
RAM 8 GB DDR4
Maximum Memory Usage 7 GB
Graphics Intel UHD or Iris Xe Integrated Graphics
Storage 256 GB SSD
Operating System Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
GPU No discrete GPU allowed

Any submission exceeding the 7 GB RAM limit during evaluation will be immediately disqualified.

African Language Bonus

Projects demonstrating meaningful support for at least one African language receive an additional 15% panel score bonus.

This encourages participants to develop AI systems that better reflect Africa’s linguistic diversity while improving accessibility for local communities.

Competition Timeline

The competition consists of three evaluation stages.

Gate 1 – Submission Package

Deadline: August 25, 2026

Participants must submit:

  • Open-source GitHub repository
  • Structured REPORT.md
  • Screenshots or demonstration clips
  • Two-minute demonstration video
  • Bonus documentation (African language support or budget laptop testing)

Gate 2 – Activities and Technical Audit

Dates: September 8 – September 29, 2026

Selected teams will participate in:

  • 30-minute technical Q&A
  • Reproducibility audit
  • Reviewer clarification
  • Optional benchmark updates
  • Optional feedback responses

Gate 3 – Final Package

Deadline: October 17, 2026

Finalists must prepare:

  • Maximum 10-slide pitch deck
  • Live presentation attendance
  • Technical setup verification

Scoring Criteria

Every submission undergoes standardized benchmarking using the official ADTC hardware profile.

Accuracy – 50%

Judges evaluate:

  • Automated benchmark performance
  • Prompt quality
  • Model correctness
  • Overall reasoning ability

Speed – 30%

Measured according to token generation speed relative to the fastest submission.

Efficiency – 20%

Rewards lower RAM usage during execution.

Lower memory consumption results in higher efficiency scores.

Additional Rules

Thermal Penalty

Teams lose 10 points if:

  • CPU temperature exceeds 85°C
  • Thermal throttling occurs

Automatic Disqualification

Submissions are immediately disqualified if:

  • The application crashes
  • Out-of-memory errors occur
  • RAM exceeds 7 GB

Performance Bonuses

Participants can further improve their scores through:

  • Budget Hardware Profile Bonus (+10%)
  • African Language Bonus (+15%)

Local Benchmarking Tool

To help participants prepare for official evaluation, ADTF provides an open-source local profiling tool that measures:

  • CPU utilization
  • Memory usage
  • Latency
  • Throughput
  • Overall hardware compatibility

This enables teams to optimize performance before submission.

Prize Pool

The competition offers a total prize pool of $20,000, along with additional technical and ecosystem support.

Grand Prize

The winning team receives:

  • $8,000 cash
  • Six-month scale-up residency
  • Venture Demo Day participation
  • Pilot matchmaking
  • ADTC Certified Trust-Mark
  • Governance and legal mentorship
  • Product hardening mentorship

Runner-Up

Prize includes:

  • $4,000 cash
  • Three-month residency
  • Pilot matchmaking
  • Venture Demo Day access

Best Integration Award

Awarded to the strongest cross-disciplinary solution.

Prize:

  • $3,000 cash

Best Localisation Award

Recognizes outstanding African language or local context integration.

Prize:

  • $1,500 cash

GPU Credits

Finalists

  • $250 GPU cloud credits
  • Up to ten finalists

Semi-finalists

  • $50 GPU cloud credits
  • Up to twenty semi-finalists

Ecosystem Partners

The competition is supported by a growing ecosystem of organizations dedicated to strengthening Africa’s deep technology landscape.

Partners include organizations across:

  • AI research
  • Venture development
  • Technology communities
  • Innovation hubs
  • Open-source communities
  • Developer networks

Frequently Asked Topics

Participants can expect guidance on topics such as:

  • Offline model evaluation
  • Hardware benchmarking
  • African language eligibility
  • Cross-disciplinary integration
  • Open-source model usage
  • Quantization tools
  • Deployment frameworks
  • Model size limitations
  • Accuracy benchmarks
  • Thermal monitoring
  • Hybrid versus offline architectures
  • Video demonstration requirements

How to Participate

Entering the challenge involves three simple steps:

Step 1

Register your project through the official submission platform.

Step 2

Work individually or build a team of up to three members.

Step 3

Read the competition rules, use the submission template, benchmark your model locally, and submit your complete Gate 1 package before the deadline.

Important Dates at a Glance

  • Gate 1 Submission Deadline: August 25, 2026
  • Technical Audit: September 8 – September 29, 2026
  • Final Package Deadline: October 17, 2026

To learn more about the opportunity Visit HERE.

Conclusion

The Africa Deep Tech Challenge 2026 represents an ambitious effort to redefine how artificial intelligence is developed and deployed across Africa. By focusing on lightweight, offline-capable AI systems that run on affordable consumer laptops, the competition seeks to remove barriers associated with cloud computing, internet dependence, and expensive hardware.

Beyond the attractive cash prizes, participants gain access to mentorship, technical validation, investor exposure, venture support, and recognition within Africa’s rapidly expanding deep technology ecosystem. Whether you are an AI researcher, software engineer, startup founder, student, or independent innovator, this challenge provides an opportunity to contribute practical AI solutions designed specifically for the realities of African communities.

If you are passionate about building accessible, efficient, and impactful artificial intelligence, now is the time to begin developing your solution. Be sure to prepare your open-source project, optimize it for the official hardware requirements, and submit your Gate 1 entry before August 25, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Are you a graduate student looking to gain practical experience in healthcare leadership and operations? The Kaiser Permanente Care Delivery Master’s Internship 2026 offers an exciting opportunity to work with one of America’s leading healthcare organizations while contributing to projects that improve patient care and organizational performance.

This paid internship allows interns to collaborate with senior healthcare leaders, clinical teams, finance professionals, and operational experts on strategic initiatives that shape the future of healthcare delivery.

Summary

  • Organization: Kaiser Permanente
  • Program: Care Delivery Master’s Internship
  • Location: Pleasanton, California, USA (Hybrid)
  • Work Schedule: Full-time
  • Duration: Internship
  • Salary: $32.45–$41.99 per hour

The Care Delivery Master’s Internship is designed for graduate students who are passionate about improving healthcare systems and patient experiences.

Interns will join Kaiser Permanente’s National Operations Strategy & Execution team, where they will contribute to enterprise-wide initiatives focused on improving healthcare quality, operational efficiency, and member experience.

Projects may include strategic initiatives such as:

  • Acute Care at Home
  • Care Coordination
  • Care Continuum
  • Durable Medical Equipment

Interns will work alongside experienced healthcare professionals and senior executives while gaining valuable exposure to healthcare innovation.

  • Conduct business and operational analysis
  • Develop communication strategies
  • Collaborate with finance, operational and clinical teams

  • Analyze processes to improve healthcare performance

  • Shadow professionals across different departments

Successful interns will receive:

  • Competitive hourly salary of $32.45–$41.99

  • Exposure to executive-level healthcare strategy
  • Hybrid work flexibility
  • Professional networking opportunities
  • Career development and mentorship

  • Project management experience
  • Consulting or business analysis skills
  • Excellent interpersonal abilities
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work in collaborative environments

Target Majors

This internship is particularly suitable for students studying:

  • Public Health
  • Healthcare Administration
  • Business Administration
  • Health Systems Management
  • Health Policy

Kaiser Permanente is recognized as one of the largest integrated healthcare organizations in the United States. Interns work on projects that directly improve healthcare delivery while receiving mentorship from experienced professionals.

Location: Pleasanton, California (Hybrid)

Salary: $32.45–$41.99 per hour

Employment Type: Full-time Internship

Job Number: 1432632

Apply Here

Apply through the official Kaiser Permanente Careers website.

If you are a graduate student seeking practical experience in healthcare operations and strategic leadership, the Kaiser Permanente Care Delivery Master’s Internship 2026 is an outstanding opportunity. Beyond competitive pay, interns gain hands-on experience working on initiatives that improve patient care, healthcare efficiency, and organizational performance. This internship provides an excellent platform to build professional skills, expand your network, and launch a successful career in healthcare administration and operations.

Discover more internship opportunities on the OFY webpage.

item.content:encoded:
If you are a highly analytical student with a passion for mathematics, quantitative finance, technology, and financial markets, the Five Rings Summer Intern 2027 – Quantitative Trader Internship offers one of the most competitive internship opportunities in the trading industry. Hosted by Five Rings, a leading proprietary trading firm with offices in New York, Boca Raton, London, and Amsterdam, this prestigious internship provides students with hands-on experience in quantitative trading, research, and strategy development while working alongside some of the industry’s brightest professionals.

The internship is based in New York City and runs for nine weeks, from the beginning of June through the beginning of August 2027. In addition to gaining invaluable industry experience, interns receive an annualized base salary of $300,000, a sign-on bonus, and corporate housing during the internship.

One of the most exciting aspects of this opportunity is that students from outside the United States are also eligible to apply, making it an excellent opportunity for talented students from around the world to launch a career in quantitative trading.

About Five Rings

Five Rings is a proprietary trading firm founded with the vision of combining strategy, innovation, and technology to compete successfully in today’s increasingly complex global financial markets.

The firm actively trades across numerous domestic and international financial markets, including both traditional and niche markets. By leveraging advanced quantitative research, sophisticated technology, and innovative trading strategies, Five Rings continually identifies new market opportunities while carefully evaluating associated risks and rewards.

With offices in:

  • New York, USA
  • Boca Raton, USA
  • London, United Kingdom
  • Amsterdam, Netherlands

Five Rings has built a reputation for fostering an open, collaborative culture where ideas and knowledge flow freely across teams.

The company believes that innovation comes from collaboration, encouraging employees and interns alike to contribute ideas, solve challenging problems, and continuously learn from one another.

About the Summer Internship Program

The Five Rings Summer Internship Program is an intensive nine-week internship designed to immerse students in the fast-paced world of quantitative trading.

Interns are not treated as observers—they become active contributors, working alongside experienced traders on real research and development projects that influence trading strategies and market decisions.

Throughout the internship, participants receive mentorship from experienced professionals while developing technical and analytical skills that prepare them for future careers in quantitative finance and proprietary trading.

Internship Duration

The internship runs:

  • Beginning of June 2027
  • Beginning of August 2027

Total duration:

  • 9 weeks

Location:

  • New York City, United States

What Interns Will Do

Participants will gain practical experience across multiple aspects of quantitative trading.

Responsibilities include:

  • Working closely with experienced traders.
  • Assisting with quantitative research projects.
  • Participating in trading strategy development.
  • Supporting research and development initiatives.
  • Analyzing financial market behavior.
  • Evaluating trading opportunities.
  • Learning risk management techniques.
  • Collaborating on innovative trading solutions.
  • Applying quantitative methods to real-world market challenges.

Interns will be encouraged to think critically, ask questions, and contribute ideas throughout the program.

Training and Learning Opportunities

The internship combines practical work with structured learning.

Participants will benefit from:

Classroom Instruction

Interns attend educational sessions covering key concepts in:

  • Quantitative trading
  • Financial markets
  • Market microstructure
  • Trading strategies
  • Risk management
  • Decision-making

Strategy Games

The program includes specially designed in-house strategy games that help interns develop:

  • Analytical thinking
  • Competitive decision-making
  • Strategic planning
  • Problem-solving skills

Mock Trading

Participants practice trading in simulated environments before applying concepts to real-world projects.

Mock trading sessions help interns understand:

  • Market dynamics
  • Trading execution
  • Risk assessment
  • Strategy evaluation

Educational Talks

Interns participate in presentations introducing:

  • Trading fundamentals
  • Quantitative research
  • Financial modeling
  • Market behavior
  • Proprietary trading concepts

Mentorship

Each intern receives direct mentorship from experienced full-time traders.

Mentors provide guidance on:

  • Research projects
  • Trading concepts
  • Career development
  • Technical skills
  • Problem-solving
  • Professional growth

This close interaction allows interns to gain valuable insights from professionals actively working in global financial markets.

Social Activities

Five Rings believes learning extends beyond the office.

Interns also participate in a variety of social and networking activities, including:

  • Strategic game nights
  • Group dinners
  • Social outings throughout New York City
  • Networking events
  • Team-building activities

These experiences help interns build strong professional relationships while enjoying the internship experience.

Benefits

Selected interns receive an outstanding compensation package that includes:

  • Annualized base salary of $300,000
  • Sign-on bonus
  • Corporate housing
  • Hands-on research experience
  • Direct mentorship
  • Classroom instruction
  • Mock trading experience
  • Strategy game participation
  • Networking opportunities
  • Professional development
  • Exposure to real financial markets

Who Can Apply?

Five Rings welcomes applications from talented and motivated students who meet the eligibility criteria.

Applicants should:

  • Be graduating in Winter 2027 or Spring/Summer 2028.
  • Have a strong quantitative background.
  • Be intellectually curious.
  • Enjoy solving challenging analytical problems.
  • Learn quickly.
  • Thrive in collaborative environments.
  • Be highly detail-oriented.
  • Demonstrate initiative and independence.
  • Be comfortable working in fast-paced environments.

APPLY HERE

Desired Skills

Successful applicants are likely to demonstrate:

  • Quantitative reasoning
  • Mathematical ability
  • Logical thinking
  • Critical thinking
  • Curiosity
  • Teamwork
  • Communication skills
  • Adaptability
  • Attention to detail
  • Strong work ethic

International Applicants

Although the internship is based in New York, Five Rings explicitly welcomes applications from students outside the United States.

This makes the internship an excellent opportunity for international students interested in gaining experience at one of the world’s leading proprietary trading firms.

Application Information

Applicants may submit applications for multiple internship positions within Five Rings.

However, the company strongly encourages candidates to apply only to the position that best aligns with their interests and career goals.

Salary

The internship offers one of the most competitive compensation packages available for students.

Compensation includes:

  • Annualized Base Salary: $300,000
  • Sign-on bonus
  • Corporate housing

Why You Should Apply

This internship offers an exceptional opportunity to:

  • Gain hands-on experience in quantitative trading.
  • Learn directly from experienced traders.
  • Work on real-world research projects.
  • Develop advanced analytical skills.
  • Build expertise in financial markets.
  • Receive outstanding mentorship.
  • Expand your professional network.
  • Experience life in New York City.
  • Strengthen your resume with experience at a globally recognized proprietary trading firm.
  • Earn one of the highest-paying internship salaries in the finance industry.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Five Rings Summer Intern 2027  Quantitative Trader Internship in New York

Deadline

Application Deadline: Not Specified (Applications are currently open).

Interested students are encouraged to apply as early as possible, as positions are expected to be highly competitive.

Conclusion

The Five Rings Summer Intern 2027 – Quantitative Trader Internship is an outstanding opportunity for ambitious students seeking a career in quantitative finance, trading, or financial technology. With a remarkable annualized salary of $300,000, additional sign-on bonus, corporate housing, world-class mentorship, and hands-on experience working on real trading strategies, the program provides a strong foundation for launching a successful career in the financial markets.

Whether you are based in the United States or studying internationally, this internship offers a rare chance to work with one of the industry’s leading proprietary trading firms while developing the technical, analytical, and professional skills needed to excel in quantitative trading. Eligible students are encouraged to submit their applications as soon as possible.

item.content:encoded:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming nearly every aspect of society, from education and employment to healthcare, governance, and civic participation. As AI technologies continue to influence public life, organizations around the world are working to ensure these systems remain transparent, accountable, and centered on human dignity.

The Data & Society Research Institute is currently inviting applications for the position of Senior Researcher, AI Civics, offering an exciting opportunity for experienced researchers passionate about artificial intelligence, civic engagement, public policy, and participatory research. This fully remote position is designed for professionals who want to shape how communities engage with AI while producing impactful research that influences public understanding and democratic governance.

The successful candidate will play a leading role in a groundbreaking two-year AI Civics program that aims to empower communities, strengthen civic participation, and create practical resources that enable the public to influence AI governance.

Applications close on July 30, 2026.

About Data & Society Research Institute

Data & Society is an independent nonprofit research organization dedicated to studying the social impacts of data-driven technologies and automation.

The institute recognizes that while technologies such as Artificial Intelligence offer tremendous opportunities, they can also create significant challenges, including:

  • Privacy violations
  • Algorithmic discrimination
  • Unequal access to opportunities
  • Social inequality
  • Community harm
  • Reduced public accountability

Through rigorous research, inclusive collaboration, and evidence-based policymaking, the organization works toward ensuring that technological innovation benefits society while protecting human rights and democratic values.

About the AI Civics Program

The AI Civics Program is a newly launched initiative focused on helping communities actively shape how Artificial Intelligence is designed, governed, and deployed.

Rather than allowing AI systems to evolve without public participation, this initiative seeks to strengthen democratic involvement by developing practical civic tools that enable communities to influence AI policies and technology governance.

The program aims to:

  • Increase public participation in AI governance
  • Build community control over AI technologies
  • Develop educational toolkits
  • Produce training resources
  • Support community organizations
  • Strengthen civic networks across the United States
  • Build a national coalition advocating for democratic accountability in AI

Working closely with national partner organizations, the program will use participatory approaches to ensure that community voices directly influence the future of AI governance.

Position Overview

Job Title: Senior Researcher, AI Civics

Organization: Data & Society Research Institute

Work Location: Fully Remote (United States)

Program Duration:

  • Expected Start: September 2026
  • Expected End: May 31, 2028

This is a two-year fixed-term position with no expectation of extension.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Program Director and will become one of the lead researchers driving the AI Civics initiative.

Salary and Employee Benefits

Successful candidates will receive an attractive compensation package.

Annual Salary

  • $78,000–$97,000 per year
  • Salary is determined based on:
    • Experience
    • Skills
    • Qualifications
    • Market considerations
    • Organizational budget
    • Internal salary equity

Employee Benefits

Employees are eligible for an excellent benefits package that includes:

  • Medical insurance
  • Dental insurance
  • Vision insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Paid federal holidays
  • 401(k) retirement management
  • Additional optional insurance products
  • Other employee support services

What You Will Do

The Senior Researcher will lead mission-critical research projects while working closely with community organizations, policymakers, researchers, and educators.

The role combines:

  • Research
  • Partnership development
  • Civic engagement
  • Policy analysis
  • Curriculum design
  • Public education
  • Community collaboration

Primary Responsibilities

1. Lead Participatory Research Projects

The successful candidate will:

  • Build and maintain relationships with community organizations
  • Conduct participatory action research
  • Collaborate with civic organizations
  • Engage local leaders
  • Support public sector stakeholders
  • Coordinate research partnerships

2. Develop Educational Resources

One of the major responsibilities involves co-creating practical resources that communities can use to better understand and influence AI systems.

These include:

  • AI toolkits
  • Facilitation guides
  • Educational curricula
  • Community training resources
  • Templates
  • Learning materials

3. Conduct Community-Based Research

The researcher will:

  • Design research methodologies
  • Collect qualitative data
  • Analyze findings
  • Produce evidence-based recommendations
  • Improve educational materials using community feedback

4. Produce High-Impact Publications

The position requires producing a variety of research outputs, including:

  • Case studies
  • Academic papers
  • Research reports
  • Public policy briefs
  • Educational publications
  • Blog articles
  • Public-facing essays
  • Lectures

5. Facilitate Workshops

Working alongside the Program Director, the Senior Researcher will help organize:

  • Co-design workshops
  • Community engagement sessions
  • Train-the-trainer programs
  • Participatory research activities
  • Capacity-building events

6. Build Strategic Partnerships

The successful candidate will help expand the AI Civics network by:

  • Identifying new collaborators
  • Building relationships with organizations
  • Coordinating research partnerships
  • Supporting civic coalitions

7. Coordinate Internal Research Activities

Responsibilities include:

  • Working with internal research teams
  • Participating in seminars
  • Joining research meetings
  • Supporting organizational learning
  • Contributing to interdisciplinary collaboration

8. Support Communications

The role also includes helping communicate with AI Civics partners by preparing:

  • Program updates
  • Event announcements
  • Meeting summaries
  • Partnership communications

9. Assist Fundraising Activities

The Senior Researcher will contribute to fundraising by:

  • Supporting grant applications
  • Drafting proposal materials
  • Working with the Development Team
  • Identifying future funding opportunities

10. Contribute to Organizational Development

Researchers are expected to actively participate in organizational life through:

  • Staff meetings
  • Research seminars
  • Reading groups
  • Internal workshops
  • Retreats
  • Town halls
  • Diversity initiatives
  • Professional development

Required Qualifications

item.content:encoded:
The UNESCO Doctoral Internships 2026–2027 present an outstanding opportunity for doctoral researchers at University College London (UCL) to gain international research experience while contributing to one of UNESCO’s flagship education initiatives. Hosted at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, these six-month research internships will allow successful applicants to work directly with the Global Happy Schools Initiative, a UNESCO-led programme dedicated to promoting educational equity, wellbeing, peace, inclusion, and values-based education around the world.

Developed through the partnership between UNESCO’s Happy Schools Initiative and UCL’s Grand Challenge of Inequalities, the internships provide doctoral students with the opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research addressing some of today’s most pressing educational challenges, including peacebuilding, community learning, social cohesion, displacement, and educational inequalities.

Successful interns will receive financial support toward accommodation in Paris and travel between London and Paris, making this a valuable opportunity for doctoral students interested in international education, public policy, educational research, and sustainable development.

About the UNESCO Doctoral Internship Programme

UNESCO is inviting applications from doctoral students currently enrolled at University College London (UCL) to participate in one of two research internships focused on advancing the Global Happy Schools Initiative.

The internships are designed to explore how education systems can create learning environments that foster:

  • Educational equity
  • Student and teacher wellbeing
  • Peacebuilding
  • Social cohesion
  • Community engagement
  • Democratic participation
  • Inclusive education
  • Lifelong learning

Interns will be based at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, where they will work alongside experts involved in implementing and expanding the Global Happy Schools Initiative.

The placements are expected to begin no later than March 2027 and will run for six months.

What is the UNESCO Global Happy Schools Initiative?

The Global Happy Schools Initiative is a UNESCO-led programme that promotes educational environments where wellbeing, equity, inclusion, and values-based learning become central components of school systems.

Rather than measuring success solely through academic performance, the initiative recognizes that thriving schools are built through positive relationships, supportive learning environments, inclusive practices, and community participation.

The initiative seeks to improve both wellbeing and educational outcomes by creating schools where learners, educators, and communities can flourish together.

The Four Pillars of the Happy Schools Framework

At the heart of the initiative is the Happy Schools Framework, which organizes positive learning environments around four interconnected pillars.

1. People

This pillar focuses on:

  • Positive relationships
  • Emotional wellbeing
  • Social-emotional learning
  • Respect
  • Positive attitudes
  • Strong teacher-student relationships

Research demonstrates that healthy interpersonal relationships contribute significantly to improved learning outcomes and student wellbeing.

2. Process

This pillar emphasizes:

  • Balanced curricula
  • Active learning
  • Innovative teaching approaches
  • Holistic assessment methods
  • Student-centered pedagogies

Rather than relying solely on examinations, the framework promotes learning experiences that encourage participation, creativity, and critical thinking.

3. Place

The Place pillar focuses on creating supportive learning environments through:

  • Inclusive schools
  • Safe physical spaces
  • Accessible digital learning
  • Community-centered education
  • Welcoming school environments

These environments encourage collaboration, inclusion, and lifelong learning.

4. Principles

The Principles pillar promotes:

  • Trust
  • Inclusion
  • Empowerment
  • Democratic participation
  • Equity
  • Shared values

Together, these principles create school cultures where every learner feels valued and supported.

Countries Already Participating

The Happy Schools Initiative has already been launched in several countries, including:

  • Portugal
  • Viet Nam
  • Japan
  • Lao People’s Democratic Republic
  • Thailand

The initiative continues to expand internationally as UNESCO works with governments and education partners worldwide.

Internship Duration

The selected interns will complete:

  • Six-month research placement
  • Based at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris
  • Expected to begin no later than March 2027

Financial Support

Successful applicants will receive financial assistance from UCL, including:

  • Contribution toward accommodation costs in Paris
  • Support for travel between London and Paris

This funding helps reduce the financial burden associated with undertaking an international research placement.

Visa Support

As the internships will take place in France, successful applicants will receive visa guidance from the French Embassy.

Participants will be required to apply for a French student trainee visa through the French Consulate because they will not be enrolled in a French higher education institution during the internship.

The Embassy will provide:

  • Information on visa requirements
  • Guidance throughout the application process
  • Support regarding relevant French visa procedures

Internship Opportunity 1: Pedagogies for Peace and the Happy Schools Initiative

The first internship focuses on understanding how the Happy Schools Framework can be expanded into settings affected by:

  • Armed conflict
  • Forced displacement
  • Social inequality
  • Fragile communities
  • Economic disadvantage

The research seeks to explore how schools can become spaces that actively promote:

  • Peacebuilding
  • Democratic participation
  • Social cohesion
  • Inclusive education
  • Conflict-sensitive teaching

This internship investigates how educational environments can contribute to peaceful societies through values-based education.

Areas of Focus

The internship includes:

  • Research into peace education
  • Analysis of educational inequalities
  • Examination of displacement contexts
  • Democratic participation in schools
  • Social cohesion initiatives

Internship Opportunity 2: Community Learning Hubs and the Happy Schools Initiative

The second internship explores one of the newest components of the Happy Schools Framework—the concept of Community Learning Hubs.

UNESCO’s recent Working Paper No. 19 established five principles connecting community learning hubs to the Happy Schools Framework.

However, UNESCO notes that there is still limited evidence demonstrating how schools actually implement these principles in practice.

This internship therefore aims to investigate:

  • How schools operationalize Community Hub principles
  • Which Happy Schools pillars support community engagement
  • Challenges schools encounter when functioning as community hubs
  • Ways multi-service community hubs can implement the Happy Schools Framework

Key Research Questions

The second internship will explore questions such as:

  • How are Community Hubs implemented in schools using the Happy Schools Framework?
  • Which of the four pillars most effectively support community learning?
  • What barriers prevent schools from functioning as community hubs?
  • How can non-school community hubs adopt the Happy Schools Framework?

What Interns Will Gain

Participants will benefit from:

  • International research experience
  • Direct collaboration with UNESCO experts
  • Exposure to global education policy
  • Experience conducting applied educational research
  • Professional networking
  • International work experience
  • Practical understanding of education for sustainable development
  • Research skills in education and public policy

Why This Internship Matters

Education systems worldwide face increasing challenges related to:

  • Conflict
  • Displacement
  • Inequality
  • Mental wellbeing
  • Community resilience
  • Social cohesion

The UNESCO Doctoral Internships provide researchers with an opportunity to contribute directly to solutions that improve learning environments for millions of learners globally.

By supporting research into Happy Schools, peace education, and community learning, interns become part of UNESCO’s broader effort to create equitable, inclusive, and sustainable education systems.

Click HERE to learn more.

How to Apply

Interested doctoral students should:

  1. Review the internship descriptions.
  2. Choose the internship that best aligns with their research interests.
  3. Complete the online application form.
  4. Submit the application before the stated deadline.

Applicants are encouraged to prepare a strong application highlighting:

  • Doctoral research interests
  • Academic achievements
  • Relevant educational research experience
  • Interest in UNESCO’s mission
  • Motivation for participating

Application Deadline

The application deadline for both internships is:

Friday, 28 August 2026 at 17:00

Late applications may not be considered.

Click HERE to apply.

Conclusion

The UNESCO Doctoral Internships 2026–2027 offer an exceptional opportunity for UCL doctoral students to contribute to one of UNESCO’s most innovative global education initiatives while gaining valuable international research experience in Paris. Through six months of immersive research at UNESCO Headquarters, interns will help shape future educational policies centered on wellbeing, peace, inclusion, and community learning.

With financial assistance for travel and accommodation, expert mentorship, and the opportunity to work alongside leading education specialists, these internships provide an outstanding platform for doctoral researchers seeking to make a meaningful contribution to global education while strengthening their academic and professional careers.

Click HERE for more internship opportunities.

Are you an experienced community development professional with extensive knowledge of U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) programs? If so, ICF is currently seeking applications for the position of Community Development Consultant (On-Call).

This remote, nationwide opportunity allows qualified professionals to join one of the world’s leading advisory and technology services firms while supporting the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). As part of ICF’s team of experts, successful candidates will provide consulting, technical assistance, training, and policy guidance to public agencies and organizations responsible for implementing critical housing and community development programs.

This position is ideal for experienced consultants, community development practitioners, workforce development professionals, public policy experts, and HUD specialists looking for a flexible, part-time consulting role with meaningful national impact.

About ICF

ICF is a globally recognized advisory and technology services company that partners with governments, businesses, and nonprofit organizations to solve complex challenges and create sustainable solutions.

The organization combines deep industry expertise with innovative technologies to help clients improve communities, strengthen public services, and deliver measurable results.

ICF is committed to creating a workplace where collaboration, innovation, diversity, and inclusion enable employees to thrive while making a positive difference in communities across the United States and around the world.

ICF is recruiting an On-Call Community Development Consultant to support the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

This is a remote, home-based position with variable part-time hours. Assignments are provided on a demand-response basis, meaning work schedules will vary depending on project requirements and client needs.

The successful consultant will work alongside a multidisciplinary team delivering technical assistance and training related to:

  • Section 3 requirements
  • Federal Labor Standards
  • Davis-Bacon requirements
  • Workforce development initiatives

  • Educational resources

Education

    • Public Administration
    • Urban Planning
    • Public Policy
    • Government
    • Related discipline

OR

Experience

  • Minimum of 10 years of professional experience in a closely related field.

Applicants must also have:

  • At least 10 years of experience working with HUD programs.
  • Extensive understanding of:
    • Section 3 requirements
    • Davis-Bacon labor standards
  • Proven experience developing and delivering:
    • Trainings
    • Workshops
    • Webinars
    • Program evaluations
    • Technical assistance
    • Public presentations

item.content:encoded:
The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers has officially opened applications for one of the most prestigious global Internet governance programs—the ICANN87 Fellowship. This fully funded international fellowship provides individuals from around the world with the opportunity to participate in high-level global discussions shaping the future of the Internet.

About the ICANN87 Fellowship Program

The ICANN Fellowship Program is designed to strengthen global participation in Internet governance by supporting individuals from underserved and underrepresented communities. The ICANN87 edition is tied to the Annual General Meeting scheduled for 17–22 October 2026 in Muscat, Oman .

This fellowship allows selected participants to:

  • Attend the ICANN Public Meeting (in-person or virtually)
  • Receive mentorship from experienced professionals
  • Gain deep insight into how global Internet systems are coordinated
  • Build international networks with experts, policymakers, and stakeholders

ICANN plays a critical role in coordinating unique Internet identifiers globally, ensuring the Internet remains stable, secure, and unified.

Fellowship Benefits (What You Will Gain)

The ICANN87 Fellowship is widely recognized as a fully funded opportunity, offering:

  • International travel support (airfare)
  • Hotel accommodation
  • Daily stipend and meals
  • Access to exclusive ICANN training programs
  • Mentorship from global experts
  • Participation in high-level policy discussions
  • Networking with global Internet leaders

Participants are also exposed to real-world policy development processes and are encouraged to contribute to ICANN’s global community even after completing the program.

Who Can Apply? (Eligible Categories of Applicants)

This fellowship is open to a broad global audience, including:

  • Students and recent graduates
  • Professionals in ICT, law, policy, cybersecurity, or related fields
  • Civil society members
  • Government representatives
  • Academic researchers
  • Entrepreneurs in the tech ecosystem

Eligible Countries and Regions

The ICANN Fellowship is global and inclusive, meaning:

  • Applicants from all countries and continents can apply
  • Special consideration is given to:
    • Individuals from developing countries
    • Underserved or underrepresented communities
    • Regions with limited participation in Internet governance

This makes it an excellent opportunity for applicants from Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East.

Eligibility Requirements

To qualify for the ICANN87 Fellowship, applicants must:

  • Be at least 21 years old
  • Demonstrate interest or involvement in:
    • Internet governance
    • Domain Name System (DNS)
    • Digital policy or cybersecurity
  • Be willing to:
    • Participate in all fellowship activities
    • Attend the ICANN Public Meeting
    • Complete required ICANN Learn courses
  • Show motivation to contribute to ICANN’s multistakeholder model

Applicants should also not be currently engaged in conflicting ICANN-supported travel programs.

Program Responsibilities

Selected fellows are expected to:

  • Participate in pre-meeting training sessions
  • Attend all fellowship sessions during the ICANN meeting
  • Engage in mentorship activities
  • Network with global stakeholders
  • Complete post-meeting evaluations

These responsibilities ensure that fellows gain maximum value and contribute meaningfully to the ICANN ecosystem.

Required Documents

Applicants must prepare the following:

  • Updated CV or Resume
  • Completed online application form
  • Proof of interest or experience in Internet governance
  • ICANN Learn course completion certificates
  • Supporting documents (optional but recommended)

All applications must be submitted through the official ICANN application portal.

Selection Criteria

Applications are evaluated based on:

  • Diversity: Representation and financial need
  • Experience: Academic or professional background
  • Motivation: Interest in ICANN’s mission
  • Potential Impact: Ability to contribute to global Internet policy

ICANN places strong emphasis on inclusivity and capacity building.

Why You Should Apply

The ICANN Fellowship is more than just a funded trip—it is a gateway to:

  • Global policy influence
  • Career advancement in tech and governance
  • Exposure to international decision-making platforms
  • Long-term engagement in Internet governance

Participants often go on to become active contributors in shaping Internet policies worldwide.

Apply here

Application Deadline

Application deadline

21 August 2026 at 23:59 UTC

The ICANN87 Fellowship 2026 stands out as one of the most impactful global fellowships in the digital policy and Internet governance space. With full funding, global exposure, and access to top-tier experts, it offers a rare opportunity for individuals to influence the future of the Internet.

The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and UNDP has officially opened applications for the Digital@UNGA Awards 2026, a prestigious global awards programme that celebrates outstanding digital initiatives, innovative policies, transformative technologies, and visionary leaders who are driving inclusive and responsible digital transformation worldwide.

Open to all stakeholders across the globe, the Digital@UNGA Awards aim to recognize groundbreaking projects, digital solutions, public policies, and youth-led innovations that are creating measurable and sustainable impact. The awards provide an international platform to showcase initiatives that promote digital inclusion, strengthen digital governance, harness emerging technologies responsibly, and empower communities through innovation.

If you are a government institution, organization, startup, NGO, researcher, policymaker, technology company, entrepreneur, or young innovator working to build a more inclusive digital future, this is an exceptional opportunity to gain international recognition from one of the world’s leading organizations for information and communication technologies.

Application Deadline: 4 August 2026

What are the Digital@UNGA Awards?

The Digital@UNGA Awards are an international recognition programme organized by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). These awards celebrate exceptional digital achievements that contribute to building an inclusive, responsible, and people-centred digital society.

The awards are designed to:

  • Recognize impactful digital initiatives from around the world.
  • Promote responsible technological innovation.
  • Encourage inclusive digital transformation.
  • Highlight successful partnerships across sectors.
  • Strengthen international cooperation.
  • Showcase leadership in digital development.
  • Inspire governments, organizations, and innovators to create scalable digital solutions.

Rather than focusing solely on technology itself, the awards recognize initiatives that create meaningful social, economic, environmental, and governance impact through digital innovation.

About the International Telecommunication Union (ITU)

The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) is the United Nations specialized agency for information and communication technologies (ICTs).

Founded in 1865, ITU brings together:

  • 194 Member States
  • More than 1,000 companies
  • International organizations
  • Universities
  • Civil society organizations
  • Research institutions

Its mission is to advance global connectivity, promote digital inclusion, develop international ICT standards, and support countries in leveraging technology for sustainable development.

Through initiatives like the Digital@UNGA Awards, ITU continues to encourage innovation that supports the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Purpose of the Digital@UNGA Awards

The Digital@UNGA Awards seek to identify and celebrate digital innovations that demonstrate:

  • Measurable impact
  • Sustainability
  • Innovation
  • Inclusiveness
  • Responsible technology use
  • Scalability
  • Ethical digital governance
  • Strong partnerships
  • Community empowerment
  • Long-term benefits for society

The programme aims to elevate initiatives that contribute to a digital future where technology benefits everyone, especially underserved and vulnerable populations.

Who Can Apply?

The Digital@UNGA Awards are remarkably inclusive and welcome submissions from all stakeholders worldwide.

Applicants may include:

  • Governments
  • Public institutions
  • Private companies
  • Startups
  • Non-governmental organizations
  • Civil society organizations
  • Academic institutions
  • Research organizations
  • International organizations
  • Technology innovators
  • Entrepreneurs

item.content:encoded:
Organizations and changemakers around the world now have an exciting opportunity to secure funding through the Resilient Futures Call 2026, a global grant initiative supporting innovative, non-partisan solutions that strengthen democratic political leadership while advancing climate resilience. Co-funded by the Better Politics Fund, European Climate Foundation, Naia Trust, and Vibe Fund, the Resilient Futures Call aims to empower individuals and organizations developing bold ideas that address one of today’s most pressing global challenges: building resilient democracies capable of responding effectively to climate change.

With a total funding pool of USD 700,000, the initiative offers two distinct funding opportunities—Ideation Grants and Incubation Grants—designed to support projects at different stages of development. Whether you have an innovative concept ready to be tested or an evidence-based initiative prepared for expansion, this funding opportunity provides significant financial support and international recognition.

About the Resilient Futures Call 2026

The Resilient Futures Call is an international funding initiative established to encourage practical, innovative, and scalable solutions that bridge two increasingly important areas:

  • Democratic political leadership
  • Climate resilience

The initiative recognizes that effective democratic institutions play a critical role in addressing climate-related challenges. By investing in organizations and individuals working at this intersection, the fund seeks to strengthen governance systems while supporting resilient communities worldwide.

Rather than supporting partisan political agendas, the program specifically funds non-partisan initiatives that contribute to healthier democratic processes and stronger climate adaptation strategies.

The 2026 funding round is jointly supported by:

  • Better Politics Fund
  • European Climate Foundation (ECF)
  • Naia Trust
  • Vibe Fund

Together, these organizations aim to encourage innovative approaches that can inspire systemic change across different regions of the world.

Total Funding Available

The Resilient Futures Call has allocated a total of:

USD 700,000

Funding is distributed through two separate grant streams:

  1. Ideation Grants
  2. Incubation Grants

Each stream serves projects at different stages of development, ensuring support for both emerging ideas and more mature initiatives.

Funding Stream 1: Ideation Grants

The Ideation Grants are designed for innovators with bold, creative, and original ideas that have the potential to make a significant impact.

These grants are ideal for applicants who are still exploring new approaches or testing innovative concepts.

Grant Amount

Successful applicants may receive funding ranging from:

  • USD 10,000
  • Up to USD 20,000

The funding is intended to help recipients transform promising ideas into practical initiatives capable of creating meaningful change.

Who Should Apply?

Ideation Grants are suitable for:

  • Individuals
  • Organizations
  • Civil society groups
  • Non-profit organizations
  • Community organizations
  • Innovation teams

Applicants may come from anywhere in the world.

The program welcomes applicants who possess:

  • New ideas
  • Creative approaches
  • Innovative concepts
  • Experimental solutions
  • Fresh perspectives on democratic leadership and climate resilience

Application Process

Applicants interested in the Ideation Grants must submit their proposals through the official online application form.

Applications will be reviewed according to the program’s objectives, innovation, relevance, and potential impact.

Decision Timeline

Successful applicants will be notified during:

Late November to Early December 2026

Funding Stream 2: Incubation Grants

The Incubation Grants support initiatives that have already moved beyond the experimental stage.

These grants are intended for organizations and individuals whose ideas have demonstrated success but require additional investment to expand, strengthen operations, or increase their impact.

Unlike the Ideation Grants, these projects should already have evidence supporting their effectiveness.

Grant Amount

Recipients may receive grants of:

Up to USD 50,000

The funding can help organizations:

  • Scale successful initiatives
  • Expand operational capacity
  • Increase geographical reach
  • Strengthen organizational development
  • Build sustainable long-term impact

Who Is Eligible?

Incubation Grants target:

  • Organizations
  • Individuals

Applicants should have:

  • Proven concepts
  • Demonstrated impact
  • Existing evidence supporting their approach
  • Strong potential for growth

Nomination Process

Unlike the Ideation Grants, there is no public application process for the Incubation Grants.

Instead:

  • Organizations and individuals are nominated.
  • Selected nominees will be contacted directly by the program.
  • Only nominated applicants will be invited to proceed.

Decision Timeline

Funding decisions will be announced:

Late November to Early December 2026

Focus Areas

Projects supported through the Resilient Futures Call should contribute to advancing work at the intersection of:

  • Democratic leadership
  • Climate resilience
  • Civic participation
  • Good governance
  • Public engagement
  • Innovative policy solutions
  • Community resilience
  • Political innovation

The initiative seeks ideas capable of creating long-lasting, systemic improvements that benefit societies facing climate-related challenges.

Global Reach

The Resilient Futures Call is open internationally.

Organizations and individuals from around the world are encouraged to participate.

Although the program identifies several priority countries for strategic investment, applications are accepted globally.

This worldwide approach ensures that innovative ideas from diverse contexts have an opportunity to receive support.

Information Session

Applicants interested in learning more about the funding opportunity may participate in the official online information session.

Date

17 August 2026

Two sessions are available:

  • Session 1: 8:00 CET
  • Session 2: 16:00 CET

These sessions provide an opportunity to better understand:

  • Funding objectives
  • Eligibility requirements
  • Application procedures
  • Selection process
  • Questions from prospective applicants

Why Apply?

The Resilient Futures Call offers more than financial support.

Successful applicants benefit from opportunities to:

  • Turn innovative ideas into impactful projects.
  • Scale proven initiatives.
  • Strengthen organizational capacity.
  • Address global climate challenges.
  • Promote democratic leadership.
  • Build resilient communities.
  • Increase international visibility.
  • Join a growing network of changemakers.
  • Access substantial grant funding.
  • Contribute to long-term systemic change.

Key Dates

  • Information Session: 17 August 2026
  • Application Deadline (Ideation Grants): 04 September 2026
  • Funding Decisions: Late November to Early December 2026

How to Apply

Applicants should complete and submit the official online application form before the application deadline here, Application form

For additional inquiries, applicants may contact:

Email: resilientfutures@betterpolitics.foundation or click HERE

Conclusion

The Resilient Futures Call 2026 represents a remarkable opportunity for individuals and organizations committed to creating stronger democratic systems and more climate-resilient societies. By offering USD 700,000 in total funding across two grant streams, the initiative supports both early-stage innovation and the expansion of proven solutions with real-world impact.

Whether you are developing a groundbreaking idea or leading an initiative ready to scale, this global funding opportunity provides the financial resources and recognition needed to accelerate your work. Eligible applicants are encouraged to prepare their proposals carefully and submit their applications before the deadline for the Ideation Grants, while organizations with established solutions should remain attentive to nomination opportunities for the Incubation Grants.

For more GLOBAL GRANTS click HERE

item.content:encoded:
Introduction

The Big Loud 2026 Creative Strategy Internship is not just another internship—it is a gateway into one of the most exciting and fast‑moving sectors of the creative economy: the intersection of music, culture, and digital engagement. Hosted by Big Loud Rock, a label known for its innovative approach to artist development and branding, this program is designed to immerse participants in the real mechanics of how artists build their presence, connect with fans, and sustain relevance in a crowded digital landscape.

In today’s music industry, creative strategy is the backbone of success. It is no longer enough for artists to simply release music; they must cultivate a brand, tell a story, and engage audiences across multiple platforms. This internship provides aspiring professionals with the chance to learn exactly how that process unfolds. Interns will work alongside seasoned strategists, creatives, and producers, gaining exposure to content planning, social media operations, and campaign execution.

What sets this internship apart is its emphasis on mentorship and practical learning. Interns will not be relegated to passive observation; instead, they will actively contribute to projects, participate in brainstorming sessions, and assist in the execution of campaigns. By the end of the program, participants will have a comprehensive understanding of how creative workflows translate into audience growth, fan loyalty, and artist success.

For students and recent graduates who are passionate about music, digital culture, and creative communication, the Big Loud 2026 Creative Strategy Internship offers a rare opportunity to bridge academic knowledge with industry practice. It is a chance to step into the vibrant world of music marketing, to understand the nuances of audience engagement, and to build skills that will serve as a foundation for future careers in creative industries.

Internship Overview

  • Category: Internship
  • Location: Santa Monica, California (In‑Office)
  • Duration: Fall 2026
  • Commitment: Part‑time, consistent in‑office presence required
  • Reports to: Manager, Creative Strategy

This internship is structured to provide hands‑on experience in content planning, social media operations, and campaign execution. Interns will work closely with the Audience Engagement Team, supporting Creative Strategists in developing and implementing artist campaigns.

Responsibilities in Detail

1. Content Planning & Creative Support

Interns will play a vital role in shaping artist content strategies.

  • Content Calendars: Assist in building and maintaining social media schedules.
  • Pre‑Production Materials: Prepare reference decks, shot lists, and trend research.
  • Creative Meetings: Participate in brainstorming sessions and contribute ideas.
  • Trend Research: Monitor emerging formats and best practices across platforms.

2. Social Media & Audience Engagement

Interns will support the execution of artist social media campaigns.

  • Posting Workflows: Assist with daily posting across platforms.
  • Community Management: Engage with fans and foster positive interactions.
  • Performance Monitoring: Analyze metrics to identify high‑performing content.
  • Deliverable Management: Ensure schedules and deadlines are met.

3. Operational & Team Support

Interns will provide essential support to the Audience Engagement Team.

  • Documentation: Maintain organized project files and shared resources.
  • Administrative Tasks: Assist with scheduling and coordination.
  • Collaboration: Work alongside strategists, creatives, and producers.
  • Campaign Development: Observe and learn from real‑time campaign execution.

Skills and Qualifications

Essential Skills

  • Strong organizational abilities.
  • Familiarity with TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.
  • Effective communication and teamwork.
  • Adaptability in a fast‑paced environment.

Personal Attributes

  • Passion for music and digital culture.
  • Positive attitude and eagerness to learn.
  • Interest in creative strategy and artist branding.

Location Requirement

Applicants must be based in Los Angeles and available to work consistently in‑office throughout Fall 2026.

Benefits of the Internship

Direct Mentorship

Guidance from experienced Creative Strategists and Audience Engagement leadership.

Real‑World Experience

Exposure to live artist campaigns and digital strategy execution.

Creative Production Workflows

Hands‑on understanding of content creation and campaign optimization.

Career Development

Practical skills that enhance employability in creative strategy, digital marketing, and music industry roles.

Industry Context

The Role of Creative Strategy in Music

Creative strategy is essential in shaping how artists connect with audiences. It involves analyzing trends, leveraging digital platforms, and crafting narratives that resonate with fans.

Audience Engagement in the Digital Age

Fans expect direct interaction with artists. Audience engagement strategies ensure artists remain relevant and connected.

The Future of Digital Content

Emerging platforms and formats continue to reshape the industry. Interns will gain firsthand experience in adapting to these changes.

Application Process

How to Apply

  1. Prepare Your Resume: Highlight relevant experience in social media, content creation, or music projects.
  2. Submit Online: Use the application platform to upload your resume.
  3. Provide Contact Information: Include your name, email, LinkedIn profile, and phone number.
  4. Deadline: Applications must be submitted before the start of Fall 2026.

Why This Internship Matters

The Big Loud 2026 Creative Strategy Internship is more than just a temporary role. It is an investment in the future of the music industry. Interns will gain skills that are directly applicable to careers in creative strategy, digital marketing, and audience engagement.

By participating, interns will not only build technical expertise but also develop a deeper understanding of how culture and creativity intersect with technology.

Learn more and apply HERE today!

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. What is the Big Loud 2026 Creative Strategy Internship?

The Big Loud 2026 Creative Strategy Internship is a part‑time, in‑office program based in Santa Monica, California. It is designed to provide students and recent graduates with hands‑on experience in artist branding, social media operations, and audience engagement. Interns will work closely with the Audience Engagement Team under the supervision of the Manager of Creative Strategy.

2. Who can apply for this internship?

Applicants must be based in Los Angeles and available to work consistently in‑office during Fall 2026. The program is open to students and recent graduates who are passionate about music, digital culture, and creative strategy.

3. What kind of work will interns be doing?

Interns will assist with:

  • Building and maintaining social content calendars.
  • Preparing pre‑production materials such as shot lists and trend research.
  • Supporting daily posting workflows across artist social accounts.
  • Engaging with fans through community management initiatives.
  • Monitoring social performance and identifying high‑performing content.
  • Maintaining organized project documentation and assisting with administrative tasks.

4. Will interns manage artist rosters independently?

No. Interns will not independently manage artist rosters. Instead, they will assist across the artists assigned to their supervising Creative Strategist, ensuring they gain exposure without being solely responsible for campaign execution.

5. What skills are required to succeed in this internship?

Applicants should have:

  • Strong organizational skills.
  • Familiarity with platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.
  • Effective communication and teamwork abilities.
  • A positive attitude and adaptability in a fast‑paced environment.

6. What will interns gain from this experience?

Interns will benefit from:

  • Direct mentorship from experienced Creative Strategists.
  • Real‑world exposure to artist marketing and digital strategy campaigns.
  • Practical understanding of creative production workflows.
  • Career development opportunities in creative strategy, digital marketing, and the music industry.

7. Is this a paid internship?

The internship is supported by Big Loud Rock’s funding initiatives. Specific details about compensation should be confirmed during the application process.

8. How long does the internship last?

The internship runs during Fall 2026. Applicants should be prepared to commit consistently throughout the semester.

9. How do I apply?

Applicants must:

  1. Prepare a resume highlighting relevant experience.
  2. Submit the application online through the provided platform.
  3. Provide contact information including name, email, LinkedIn profile, and phone number.
  4. Upload a resume in PDF or DOCX format.

10. What is the deadline for applications?

Applications must be submitted before the start of Fall 2026. Early submission is recommended to ensure consideration.

11. What makes this internship unique compared to others?

Unlike many internships, the Big Loud 2026 Creative Strategy Internship emphasizes mentorship, collaboration, and real‑world exposure. Interns will actively contribute to projects, participate in creative discussions, and gain a comprehensive understanding of how campaigns are developed and optimized.

Visit HERE to learn more about Big Loud

Conclusion

The Big Loud 2026 Creative Strategy Internship is more than an entry‑level opportunity—it is a transformative experience that equips participants with the tools, insights, and confidence to thrive in the competitive world of music and digital engagement. By working directly with the Audience Engagement Team, interns will gain firsthand exposure to the strategies that drive artist branding, fan interaction, and content innovation.

This program is designed to nurture future leaders in creative strategy. Interns will leave with not only technical skills in content planning and social media operations but also a deeper appreciation for the cultural and technological forces that shape the music industry. They will understand how campaigns are conceived, executed, and optimized, and they will be prepared to apply these lessons in future roles across creative industries.

For those who aspire to careers in music marketing, digital content strategy, or audience development, this internship represents a critical stepping stone. It offers mentorship from experienced professionals, practical exposure to industry workflows, and the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to artist campaigns.

Ultimately, the Big Loud 2026 Creative Strategy Internship is about more than learning—it is about becoming part of a creative community, about shaping the future of how artists connect with audiences, and about investing in the next generation of creative strategists. Applicants who are passionate, adaptable, and eager to learn will find this internship to be a defining chapter in their professional journey.

To explore and lean more about other fellowship opportunities, visit the OFY page HERE.
